title_en: Choosing a Moving Company or Lorry for a Room Move
summary_en: What to check before booking a mover or lorry for a room-to-room move, and how to avoid the common pitfalls.
body_en:
Moving one room's worth of belongings doesn't need a full moving company — but it does need a plan, or you'll end up paying for extra time and trips you didn't expect. A bit of planning the week before makes the whole day go faster.

Lorry rental vs a moving company

  • A lorry with a driver is usually cheaper for a single room, especially if you and friends can help carry and pack.
  • A full moving company costs more but packs, carries and sometimes insures your items — worth it if you have fragile or heavy furniture.
  • For a single room with mostly boxes and a mattress, many renters manage with just a lorry booking.
  • Ask around your community group for a driver others have used before — a personal recommendation is often more reliable than a random online listing.

Before you book

  • Confirm whether the quote includes labour to carry items up and down, or just the drive.
  • Ask about lift access at both addresses — a flat with no lift, or a lift that's often busy, adds time and sometimes cost.
  • Check if there's a minimum charge, and what happens if the move takes longer than quoted.
  • Agree the exact pick-up and drop-off addresses in advance, so there's no confusion or extra charge on the day.

On moving day

  • Pack boxes the night before. Paying movers to wait while you pack is the easiest way to blow your budget.
  • Take photos of furniture before it's loaded, in case anything is damaged in transit.
  • Keep small valuables — passport, cash, important documents — with you, not in the lorry.

Timing it well

Avoid weekends and month-end if you can; movers are busiest and sometimes pricier then. A weekday move, even taking a half-day off work, is often smoother and cheaper.
